description:
Give each protocol callback a dispatching body synthesized from its ProtocolDispatch arms. Not yet routed -- prove it lowers, keep behavior unchanged + green.

STRATEGY (refined after reading the lowerer): synthesize the callback's SURFACE, not raw IR. Lowerer::lower (jobs/body.rs:899) builds the whole LoweredBody from a FunctionSurface's clauses (params + body Expr); plan_entry_dispatch builds the EntryDispatch from the same clauses. So synthesize a multi-clause FunctionSurface and let the EXISTING pipeline lower it + plan the matrix -- no hand-built LoweredBody/EntryDispatch.

SYNTHESIZED SURFACE for callback C, from ProtocolDispatch(protocol).arms (target ModuleId + impl FunctionId), arms ordered STRUCT-before-MAP:
  - each clause: receiver param + (n-1) var params; body = a call expr to the impl: '<impl>(receiver, ...rest)'. Reference the impl by resolved FunctionId/qualified name.
  - built-in target: receiver param carries a TYPE precondition. ':: list' resolves; ':: map' does NOT (no map type name, fz-usm). So preconditions must be injected as RESOLVED Tys, not source tokens.
  - struct target: receiver param[0] = a struct pattern '%Module{...}' (the proven path; Region::Type over a struct panics, fz-bv3). list/range route soundly; map-vs-struct soundness needs fz-bv3 (only affects map-using fixtures).

KEY EXTENSION: entry_source_patterns (jobs/dispatch.rs:278) builds preconditions by resolving clause.param_annotation TOKENS via resolve_type_expr_body. Add a path for synthesized clauses to carry a PRE-RESOLVED Ty precondition (= module_impl_target_ty(target)) directly, bypassing token resolution. This is the one surgical change; everything else reuses the lowerer + producer unchanged.

INJECTION: provide the synthesized surface as the callback's definition, derived from ProtocolDispatch(protocol) and re-derived as arms grow (built-in impls co-located -> settle together). Either synthesize the callback's FunctionSource (quoted, build_module_info_function precedent) or intercept define_function for protocol callbacks to install the synthesized surface.

SEAM SUMMARY: (1) synthesize FunctionSurface from arms; (2) install it as the callback's definition; (3) extend entry_source_patterns for pre-resolved Ty preconditions; then lower_function + plan_entry_dispatch run unchanged -> DispatchMask/Recursive/analysis derive. VERIFY: a test that Enumerable.reduce's synthesized dispatcher lowers + plans an N-arm entry dispatch; lib+matrix green (unrouted).

comments.text:
RESEARCH RESOLVED (fork + constraints):

FACT-ECOSYSTEM INSIGHT (decisive). A compiler2 function is not just a LoweredBody -- it is a whole derived fact ecosystem: FunctionSource -> ExpandedFunctionSource -> FunctionDefined(surface) -> LoweredBody -> EntryDispatch -> Recursive -> DispatchMask -> FunctionContract -> type refs -> runtime_demand. Source-level synthesis (give the callback a synthesized quoted FunctionSource) reuses this ENTIRE chain automatically; IR-level synthesis must hand-produce each fact consistently (LoweredBody + EntryDispatch + Recursive + DispatchMask + ...), which is far more surface area and risk. => Prefer SOURCE-LEVEL synthesis (build_module_info_function precedent), NOT raw IR.

ANNOTATION CONSTRAINTS (measured):
- ':: List.t' / ':: Map.t' HANG -- because List.t / Map.t are NOT defined types (no @type t in list.fz/map.fz); unresolved type -> demand loop. Incidental, not fundamental.
- Built-in type annotations dispatch correctly: ':: list', ':: map', ':: integer', ':: float', ':: atom' (verified ':: list'/':: integer'). Use these for built-in impl targets.
- Struct impls (Range) must dispatch via a STRUCT PATTERN '%Range{...}' head, NOT ':: Range.t'. The Range impl already pattern-matches '%Range{...}'. Note: '%Range{} = x' as-bind hit 'pattern as-bind lhs must be a variable' -- use plain '%Range{first: f, last: l, step: s}' field binds (as the real impl does) or a bare struct pattern with no as-bind.
- The synthesizer must therefore generate per-arm source keyed on impl-target KIND, mirroring module_impl_target_ty's built-in-name-vs-struct branch (world.rs:2900/3085): built-in name -> ':: <builtin>' annotation; struct module -> '%Module{...}' pattern.

DISPATCHER SOURCE SHAPE (per callback C with arms):
  fn <C>(x :: list, ...rest), do: <Enumerable.List.C>(x, ...rest)
  fn <C>(x :: map,  ...rest), do: <Enumerable.Map.C>(x, ...rest)
  fn <C>(%Range{...}=destructure, ...rest), do: <Enumerable.Range.C>(...)
Body calls reference the impl by its qualified name (resolvable in the protocol module namespace) or, better, the already-resolved impl FunctionId carried in the arm (ProtocolCallbackImpl.function) to avoid re-resolution.

DERIVATION: the dispatcher source is derived from ProtocolDispatch(protocol) and re-derived when arms grow (defimpls discovered lazily). Inject by making the callback's FunctionSource provider synthesize it (ensure_function_source for a protocol callback returns the synthesized dispatcher), so the rest of the pipeline (expand/define/lower/plan_entry_dispatch) runs unchanged.

VERIFIED PIPELINE: runtime type dispatch among typed clauses on a union value compiles+runs in interp AND AOT (check(x::integer)/check(_) on integer|atom). So once the callback is a typed multi-clause function, the union case works by construction.

DIRECTION CONFIRMED + FORK RESOLVED BY EXPERIMENT (do NOT abandon protocols).

A library experiment (rewriting Enumerable as a plain typed-multi-clause module) proved the TARGET shape works: runtime dispatch over a list|struct union compiles+runs (interp+AOT). It also resolved source-vs-IR decisively:
- SOURCE synthesis is blocked by LIBRARY type-name gaps: ':: list' resolves, but ':: map' -> 'unknown type name map', and List.t/Map.t/Range.t are undefined (hang). The runtime library is incomplete here.
- The COMPILER already has the exact per-impl types via world.module_impl_target_ty(target) (list/map/Range-struct) -- the same types resolve_protocol_call uses. Feed THESE straight into the matrix producer (RegionQuestion::type_region), bypassing source type-name resolution entirely.

=> SYNTHESIS = build the matrix from ProtocolDispatch arms with module_impl_target_ty(target), NOT source annotations. The defprotocol/defimpl already produce ProtocolDispatch (arms: target -> impl callback fns) = the matrix's input table.

SEAM: make the protocol callback a REAL function:
- EntryDispatch(callback): one type_region(input0, module_impl_target_ty(arm.target)) arm per impl -> outcome i. (For a struct target like Range, module_impl_target_ty returns the struct value type; VERIFY a Region::Type over the struct type dispatches a struct value at runtime -- if not, use a struct-shape arm mirroring the working '%Range{...}' pattern.)
- LoweredBody(callback): N forwarding clauses, clause i tail-calls the impl FunctionId (ProtocolCallbackImpl.function) with the whole receiver + rest (the impl destructures, as Enumerable.Range.reduce already does).
- Remove the resolve_function_call protocol_callback interception so the callback resolves as a normal single-target function; keep arm/impl-module demand.

Then concrete receiver -> reachability monomorphizes; union receiver -> runtime dispatch. The library type-name gaps (map/List.t/Map.t) are a SEPARATE cleanup (could be filed) but are NOT on the critical path once synthesis uses module_impl_target_ty.

SOURCE-vs-IR DECIDED: IR-level (build the matrix directly). Source is blocked two ways:
1. No source type-NAME for built-in collections: builtin_from_name (resolve.rs:397) has integer/float/atom/binary/bool/nil/any/... but NO 'list' and NO 'map'. ':: map' => 'unknown type name map'. (':: list' resolved via some other path but ':: map' has none.) Maps are written structurally '%{}', not by name.
2. A Region::Type arm over a STRUCT type PANICS at runtime: '%Box{}'-typed receiver dispatch emits fz_struct_get_field_ref on the wrong ValueKind (runtime/src/ir_runtime.rs:1620 ExpectedTag{expected:Struct, found:List}). So structs cannot use a type_region arm; they need a STRUCT-SHAPE arm (the '%Range{...}' pattern path, which works in the proven experiment).

THEREFORE the synthesized EntryDispatch needs TWO arm kinds, mirroring module_impl_target_ty's built-in-vs-struct branch (world.rs:2900):
- built-in target -> RegionQuestion::type_region(input0, module_impl_target_ty(target))  [exact resolved Ty, no source name]
- struct target  -> a struct-shape question replicating how Pattern::Struct lowers in dispatch_matrix::pattern (Region for struct tag + field projections as needed; the body forwards the WHOLE receiver so field binds may be unnecessary)
Reuse the matrix producer by building SourcePatternRows<Ty> with mixed preconditions(resolved Ty for built-ins) + Pattern::Struct(struct arms), fed to pattern_dispatch_from_source -- this reuses ALL producer logic including struct handling, with resolved types. Then synthesize LoweredBody = N forwarding tail-call clauses to the impl FunctionIds.

INCIDENTAL BUGS FOUND (tangential, candidate tickets): (a) Region::Type over a struct type panics instead of dispatching (runtime ir_runtime.rs:1620) -- a real codegen/runtime bug; (b) no 'list'/'map' builtin type names (library/type-system incompleteness). Neither is on the critical path since IR synthesis uses module_impl_target_ty + struct patterns.

PROGRESS (uncommitted WIP in tree, lib 1084/0 green, behavior-preserving):

DONE:
- New module src/compiler2/jobs/protocol_dispatch.rs: synthesize_callback_entry_dispatch(world, callback) -> PatternDispatchPlan<Ty>. Builds the dispatch matrix directly from ProtocolDispatch arms via pattern_dispatch_from_source: built-in target -> PatternRow with resolved-Ty precondition (Input(0), module_impl_target_ty(target)); struct target -> Pattern::Struct{module,fields:[]} (nominal); arms sorted struct-before-map. Reuses the matrix producer; needs NO source type names.
- Wired into jobs/dispatch.rs plan_entry_dispatch: protocol callbacks route to plan_protocol_callback_entry_dispatch, which waits on FactKey::ProtocolDispatch(protocol) then define_entry_dispatch from the synthesized plan. Inert at runtime today (nothing demands a callback's EntryDispatch until routing flips in fz-bin.2), so lib+matrix unchanged.
- jobs/mod.rs registers the module.

REMAINING (the forwarding BODY + provisioning; impl_function field is the next consumer -> currently one unused-field warning marks it):
1. Synthesize the callback's quoted dispatcher SOURCE (build_module_info_function pattern, src/compiler2/source.rs QuotedSourceBuilder): N clauses, clause i = 'fn <C>(x0..x{n-1}), do: <impl_i qualified name>(x0..x{n-1})' -- PLAIN var params (no type annotations, so no ':: map' issue; the dispatch comes from the intercepted plan_entry_dispatch). Qualified impl name = module_name(function_module(impl_i)) + '.' + function_ref(impl_i).name; resolves via resolve_runtime_function dotted path. CHECK builder.call handles a dotted callee name.
2. Build a FunctionSource for the callback { code: protocol module code, owner_module: protocol, namespace: world.module_scope(protocol).namespace(), capture_params:[], required_remote_macros:[], variadic:false, source: builder.root(<synthesized clauses list>) } and note it (world.note_function_source).
3. Provisioning hook: ensure_function_source(callback) (world.rs:2467) returns module-load jobs today; for a protocol callback, return a synth job (or note eagerly once ProtocolDispatch settles) that produces the source from arms. Then expand/define/lower run unchanged -> LoweredBody.
4. (fz-bin.2) remove the resolve_function_call protocol_callback interception (jobs/semantic.rs:1161) so the callback resolves as a normal single-target function -> demands its EntryDispatch/LoweredBody -> the synthesis activates.
5. Test: Enumerable.reduce lowers + plans an N-arm entry dispatch; then /tmp/listrange.fz compiles.

title: Synthesize a protocol-callback dispatcher from ProtocolDispatch arms
